children.title: Gauge-Generating Sets
children.top_down_role: Geometric classes of generating sets that determine whether the resulting model is a norm, seminorm, or asymmetric gauge.

children.title: Symmetric Convex-Body Gauges
children.top_down_role: Centrally symmetric generating bodies and their norm-like models.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Convex-Body Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Minkowski functional generated by a centrally symmetric convex body.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(C\subset X\) be compact, convex, centrally symmetric, and satisfy \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\). Its gauge is
\[\gamma_C(x):=\inf\{t\ge 0:x\in tC\}.\]
Then \(\gamma_C\) is a norm on \(X\): it is finite, convex, positively homogeneous, symmetric, and satisfies the triangle inequality and \(\gamma_C(x)=0\) only for \(x=0\). Moreover, \(C=\{x\in X:\gamma_C(x)\le 1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge of a compact, symmetric convex body containing the origin in its interior is a norm whose closed unit ball is exactly that body.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C\) is a norm and \(C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le 1\}\).

notation.meaning: scalar dilation of C by t

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and norm characterization are mathematically correct and fit the symmetric-gauge container, but no inspectable authoritative citation is supplied.

children.title: Asymmetric Convex-Body Gauges
children.top_down_role: Directional and sign-sensitive models generated by noncentrally symmetric bodies.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Convex-Body Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite directional gauge generated by a noncentrally symmetric convex body.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(C\subset X\) be compact and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\) and \(C\ne-C\). Define
\[\gamma_C(x):=\inf\{t\ge 0:x\in tC\}.\]
Then \(\gamma_C:X\to[0,\infty)\) is finite, convex, positively homogeneous, subadditive, and positive definite, and
\[C=\{x\in X:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}.\]
Because \(C\ne-C\), the gauge is not symmetric: there exists \(x\in X\) such that \(\gamma_C(x)\ne\gamma_C(-x)\). Hence \(\gamma_C\) is a gauge but not a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noncentrally symmetric convex body containing the origin in its interior generates a finite, positive-definite sublinear gauge whose values differ in some pair of opposite directions, so the gauge is not a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C\) is a finite positive-definite gauge with unit sublevel set \(C\), and it is not symmetric.

notation.meaning: asymmetric Minkowski gauge generated by C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Minkowski-functional characterization for a noncentrally symmetric convex body

children.title: Quotient-Seminorm Gauge Geometry
children.top_down_role: Models with nullspaces, invariant components, and quotient-space interpretations.

children.title: Seminorm Nullspace Geometry
children.top_down_role: Null directions and invariant components within seminorm models.

knowledge_statements.title: Seminorm Nullspace Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry induced by the kernel of a finite-dimensional seminorm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p:X\to[0,\infty)\) be a seminorm on a finite-dimensional real vector space \(X\), and define \(N:=\{x\in X:p(x)=0\}\). Then \(N\) is a linear subspace and
\[p(x+n)=p(x)\qquad(x\in X,\ n\in N).\]
For every \(r\ge0\), the sublevel set \(B_r:=\{x\in X:p(x)\le r\}\) therefore satisfies \(B_r+N=B_r\). If \(N\ne\{0\}\), each \(B_r\) is nonempty and unbounded along \(N\). Thus the seminorm value depends only on the coset \(x+N\), not on the representative within that coset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A seminorm is constant on cosets of its nullspace. Every nonnegative-radius sublevel set is invariant under nullspace translations and, when the nullspace is nontrivial, is unbounded along that nullspace.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=\ker p\) is a subspace, \(p(x+n)=p(x)\) for \(n\in N\), and \(B_r+N=B_r\) for every \(r\ge0\).

children.title: Quotient-Space Gauge Geometry
children.top_down_role: Gauge structure carried by equivalence classes in quotient spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Space Gauge Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm representation of a seminorm after quotienting by its nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\) be a seminorm on a finite-dimensional real vector space \(X\), let \(N:=\ker p\), and let \(\pi:X\to X/N\) be the quotient map. The formula
\[\bar p(\pi x):=p(x)\]
is independent of the representative \(x\) and defines a norm on \(X/N\). Moreover,
\[p=\bar p\circ\pi,\qquad \{z\in X/N:\bar p(z)\le1\}=\pi(\{x\in X:p(x)\le1\}).\]
Hence seminorm gauge geometry on \(X\) is precisely norm geometry on the quotient, lifted along \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every seminorm becomes a genuine norm on the quotient by its nullspace, and its unit ball is the quotient image of the original unit sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar p([x])=p(x)\) is a well-defined norm on \(X/N\) and \(p=\bar p\circ\pi\).

notation.meaning: canonical quotient map from X to X/N
norm induced on the quotient space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard quotient-norm construction for seminorms
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quotient-norm representation is correct, internally consistent, and appropriate for the container, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Invariant Representative Classes
children.top_down_role: Relationships among representatives that differ by nullspace components.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Representative Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative invariance for objectives and constraints that descend through a seminorm quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\) be a seminorm on \(X\) with nullspace \(N\), and write \([x]=x+N\). Then
\[p(x)=p(x+n)\qquad(n\in N),\]
so the gauge value depends only on \([x]\). More generally, a function \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) defines a function \(\bar f:X/N\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) by \(\bar f([x])=f(x)\) if and only if \(f(x+n)=f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(n\in N\). Thus any quotient-compatible model must be invariant on each representative class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function descends to the quotient exactly when it is constant on nullspace cosets; seminorm objectives automatically satisfy this representative invariance.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a seminorm on a finite-dimensional real vector space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\bar f\circ\pi\) for some \(\bar f\) if and only if \(f(x+n)=f(x)\) for all \(n\in N\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: universal factorization property of a quotient map
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representative-invariance criterion is mathematically correct and fits the container, but no authoritative quotient-space source is cited.

children.title: Quotient Descent Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting faithful passage from ambient models to quotient geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Descent Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-recovery boundary for seminorm minimization, distinguishing point recovery from recovery modulo the nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\) be a seminorm with nullspace \(N\), let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and define
\[D_p(x_\star):=\{d:\exists t>0,\ p(x_\star+td)\le p(x_\star)\}.\]
For the problem \(\min\{p(x):Ax=Ax_\star\}\), the solution class \([x_\star]\) is unique in \(X/N\) exactly when
\[\ker A\cap D_p(x_\star)\subseteq N.\]
Pointwise uniqueness instead requires \(\ker A\cap D_p(x_\star)=\{0\}\). In particular, any nonzero vector in \(N\cap\ker A\) makes exact representative recovery impossible, although quotient recovery may remain possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery modulo the seminorm nullspace requires no feasible descent direction outside that nullspace; recovering one exact representative additionally excludes feasible nullspace directions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quotient uniqueness holds iff \(\ker A\cap D_p(x_\star)\subseteq N\); pointwise uniqueness requires equality with \(\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: descent cone of p at the target

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct nullspace/descent-cone uniqueness criterion specialized to quotient recovery
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The descent-direction conditions correctly distinguish uniqueness modulo the seminorm nullspace from pointwise uniqueness, and failure_boundary is the appropriate kind. A dedicated source is required for this nontrivial exact-recovery criterion.

children.title: Extended-Valued Gauges
children.top_down_role: Gauge constructions that incorporate conic or domain restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Valued Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski gauge for a closed convex generating set that need not absorb the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, closed, convex, and contain \(0\). Define
\[\gamma_C(x):=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\},\qquad \inf\varnothing:=+\infty.\]
Then \(\gamma_C:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is convex and positively homogeneous, its effective domain is \(\operatorname{cone}C:=\bigcup_{t\ge0}tC\), and \(\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}=C\). Thus failure of \(C\) to absorb \(X\) is represented by the value \(+\infty\) outside the generated cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonabsorbing closed convex set generates a gauge that is finite on its conic hull and infinite outside it, thereby encoding domain restrictions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and contains \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}\gamma_C=\operatorname{cone}C\) and \(C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}\).

notation.meaning: union of all nonnegative dilations of C

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Extended Real-Valued Functions and Closedness p. 13

children.title: Minimum-Gauge Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Exact-data models selecting the least-complex feasible object.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Gauge Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-data convex model minimizing structural gauge over an affine measurement fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(b\in Y\), and let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a proper convex gauge. Minimum-gauge interpolation is
\[\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in X}\ \kappa(x)\qquad\operatorname{subject\ to}\qquad Ax=b.\]
Its optimal value is \(v(b):=\inf\{\kappa(x):Ax=b\}\), with \(v(b)=+\infty\) when the affine fiber contains no point in \(\operatorname{dom}\kappa\). Any minimizer is a least-gauge exact interpolant of the data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-gauge interpolation selects an exact fit with the smallest structural gauge, assigning infinite value when no gauge-finite exact fit exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(b)=\inf\{\kappa(x):Ax=b\}\), and each minimizer is a least-gauge exact interpolant.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard gauge-minimization formulation of exact interpolation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-data model is precise, and definition is an appropriate kind for this optimization-interface container, but no authoritative gauge-recovery or inverse-problems source is supplied.

children.title: Gauge-Constrained Estimation
children.top_down_role: Estimation under an explicit structural budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Constrained Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss minimization over a prescribed gauge sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(F:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a proper convex data-fidelity function, let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a proper convex gauge, and let \(\tau\ge0\). Gauge-constrained estimation is
\[\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in X}\ F(x)\qquad\operatorname{subject\ to}\qquad \kappa(x)\le\tau.\]
The parameter \(\tau\) is the structural budget. The feasible set is the convex sublevel set \(\tau\{x:\kappa(x)\le1\}\), interpreted at \(\tau=0\) directly through \(\kappa(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge-constrained estimation minimizes a convex data loss among objects whose structural gauge does not exceed a fixed budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) is a proper convex gauge and \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimator minimizes \(F\) over the convex structural budget set \(\{x:\kappa(x)\le\tau\}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained-estimation template is correct, including its separate treatment of the zero budget, but it lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Gauge-Penalized Estimation
children.top_down_role: Estimation balancing data fidelity against gauge regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Penalized Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite convex estimation with a positively weighted structural gauge penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(F:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a proper convex data-fidelity function, let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a proper convex gauge, and let \(\lambda>0\). Gauge-penalized estimation is
\[\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in X}\ F(x)+\lambda\kappa(x).\]
The coefficient \(\lambda\) fixes the relative cost of structural complexity. The objective is convex; it is proper whenever \(\operatorname{dom}F\cap\operatorname{dom}\kappa\ne\varnothing\). Any attained minimizer balances fidelity and gauge cost under this scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge-penalized estimation minimizes convex data loss plus a positive multiple of a structural gauge, producing a scalarized fidelity-complexity tradeoff.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(\kappa\) are proper convex functions, with \(\kappa\) a gauge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F+\lambda\kappa\) is a proper convex objective defining the gauge-penalized estimator.

children.title: Residual-Constrained Gauge Recovery
children.top_down_role: Models minimizing structural complexity subject to a fidelity tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Constrained Gauge Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge minimization subject to an explicit convex residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear between finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(b\in Y\), let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a proper convex gauge, let \(\rho:Y\to[0,+\infty]\) be a convex residual measure, and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Residual-constrained gauge recovery is
\[\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in X}\ \kappa(x)\qquad\operatorname{subject\ to}\qquad \rho(Ax-b)\le\varepsilon.\]
The feasible set is convex. At \(\varepsilon=0\), if \(\rho(y)=0\) exactly when \(y=0\), the model reduces to minimum-gauge interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-constrained recovery finds the least-gauge object whose predicted data lie within a prescribed convex residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) is linear between finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(\kappa\) is a proper convex gauge and \(\rho\) is a convex nonnegative residual measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model minimizes \(\kappa(x)\) over the convex set \(\{x:\rho(Ax-b)\le\varepsilon\}\).

children.title: Pareto Value-Function Correspondence

children.title: Pareto Tradeoff Curves
children.top_down_role: Tradeoff-curve organization of competing model criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Tradeoff Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-inverse relation between fidelity-budget and gauge-budget value functions under attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(F:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a data-fidelity function, and let \(\kappa:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a gauge. Define
\[\phi(\tau):=\inf\{F(x):\kappa(x)\le\tau\},\qquad \psi(\sigma):=\inf\{\kappa(x):F(x)\le\sigma\}.\]
Assume that each finite infimum appearing in these two constrained problems is attained. Then \(\phi\) and \(\psi\) are nonincreasing and satisfy
\[\psi(\sigma)=\inf\{\tau\ge0:\phi(\tau)\le\sigma\},\qquad \phi(\tau)=\inf\{\sigma\ge0:\psi(\sigma)\le\tau\},\]
with \(\inf\varnothing:=+\infty\). The corresponding attained solutions describe the same attainable lower Pareto boundary in the \((\kappa,F)\)-plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the relevant constrained optima are attained, the optimal fidelity at each gauge budget and the optimal gauge at each fidelity budget are nonincreasing generalized inverses that describe the same attainable lower Pareto boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(F\) and \(\kappa\) take values in \([0,+\infty]\), with \(\kappa\) a gauge.
Every finite infimum defining \(\phi(\tau)\) or \(\psi(\sigma)\) at the parameters under consideration is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the stated attainment condition, \(\phi\) and \(\psi\) are nonincreasing generalized inverses and describe the same attainable lower Pareto boundary.

notation.meaning: minimum fidelity at gauge budget tau
minimum gauge at fidelity budget sigma

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generalized-inverse characterization of attained constrained value functions

children.title: Value-Function Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Value-function organization of constrained or penalized model interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Parameterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained value function for a convex fidelity objective and gauge budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\tau\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
v(\tau):=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ \rho(x)\leq\tau\},
\]
with \(v(\tau)=+\infty\) when the feasible set is empty. Whenever the infimum is attained at \(x_\tau\), one has \(\rho(x_\tau)\leq\tau\) and \(f(x_\tau)=v(\tau)\). For all \(\tau_1,\tau_2\in\mathbb R\) with \(\tau_1\leq\tau_2\),
\[
v(\tau_2)\leq v(\tau_1).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The value function assigns each gauge budget the smallest attainable fidelity objective and is nonincreasing as the permitted budget grows.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(\rho:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed convex gauge and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) records the optimal fidelity achievable at each gauge budget and is nonincreasing on its effective domain.

children.title: Route Correspondence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where Pareto and value-function parameterizations identify matching models.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\rho\) are proper closed convex functions on a finite-dimensional space, with \(\rho\) a gauge.
The constrained problem at \(\tau\) attains its optimum and satisfies a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constrained and penalized routes correspond through an optimal multiplier, with the converse obtained at the attained gauge level.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT correspondence between constrained and penalized gauge routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P_\tau:=\min_x\{f(x):\rho(x)\leq\tau\},\qquad L_\lambda:=\min_x\{f(x)+\lambda\rho(x)\}.
\]
If \(x_\tau\) solves \(P_\tau\), then there exists \(\lambda_\tau\geq0\) such that \(x_\tau\) solves \(L_{\lambda_\tau}\) and \(\lambda_\tau(\rho(x_\tau)-\tau)=0\). Conversely, if \(x_\lambda\) solves \(L_\lambda\) and \(\tau=\rho(x_\lambda)\), then \(x_\lambda\) solves \(P_\tau\). A one-to-one parameter correspondence additionally requires an active constraint and sufficient uniqueness or strict monotonicity of the frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under convex regularity, an optimal multiplier maps a constrained gauge problem to a penalized one; the reverse map uses the optimizer's attained gauge.
knowledge_statements.title: Route Correspondence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimizer correspondence is standard under an appropriate convex constraint qualification, but the claim about a one-to-one parameter map uses insufficiently specified uniqueness and strict-monotonicity conditions. An authoritative source is needed to fix the exact regime.

children.title: Route Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degeneracies or discontinuities that obstruct route correspondence.

assumptions_latex: The constrained budget satisfies \(\tau>0\), while the penalty satisfies \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained and penalized solution sets differ, so no bijective correspondence between \(\tau\) and \(\lambda\) exists.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inactive constraints and nonuniqueness destroy bijective route parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the constrained route,
\[
S_\tau:=\mathop{\rm argmin}\{0:|x|\leq\tau\}=[-\tau,\tau].
\]
For the penalized route,
\[
T_\lambda:=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}\lambda|x|=\{0\}.
\]
Thus every positive budget produces a continuum of constrained minimizers, whereas every positive penalty produces only the origin. Complementary slackness permits the zero multiplier because the constraint may be inactive at an optimizer. Consequently, equality of optimal values does not imply equality of solution sets, and neither a unique multiplier nor a bijective budget-penalty map can be recovered without activity and nondegeneracy assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective with absolute-value complexity yields many constrained minimizers but only one positively penalized minimizer, preventing bijective route correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Route Failure Boundaries

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular convex regime for correspondence of budget and penalty parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible point \(x_\tau\) belongs to the parameter-correspondence regime precisely when there is \(\lambda\geq0\) such that
\[
0\in\partial f(x_\tau)+\lambda\partial\rho(x_\tau),\qquad \rho(x_\tau)\leq\tau,
\qquad \lambda(\rho(x_\tau)-\tau)=0.
\]
Then \(x_\tau\) minimizes both \(f\) over \(\{x:\rho(x)\leq\tau\}\) and \(f+\lambda\rho\) over the ambient space. If \(\lambda>0\), the gauge constraint is active. Uniqueness of the common optimizer and strict variation of the active multiplier yield a single-valued local parameter map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint qualification, KKT stationarity, complementarity, and suitable uniqueness identify the regime where budget and penalty parameterizations agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Correspondence Regimes

children.title: Parameterization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Nonuniqueness, inactive constraints, discontinuous paths, and degeneracy obstructing model equivalence.

assumptions_latex: Budgets and positive penalties parameterize constrained and penalized models, respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inactive constraints and nonunique constrained optima make the parameter-to-solution correspondence set-valued and noninvertible.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete degeneracy showing failure of optimizer-path equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\tau>0\),
\[
S(\tau):=\mathop{\rm argmin}\{f(x):\rho(x)\leq\tau\}=[-\tau,\tau],
\]
whereas for every \(\lambda>0\),
\[
T(\lambda):=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x}\{f(x)+\lambda\rho(x)\}=\{0\}.
\]
The optimizer \(x=0\) leaves the budget constraint strictly inactive, and every other constrained optimizer has no corresponding positive-penalty optimum. Hence the optimizer path is nonunique on the constrained side and constant on the penalized side. Removing activity, uniqueness, or multiplier nondegeneracy therefore invalidates any claim of invertible parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat objective makes constrained optimizers nonunique and constraints inactive, while positive penalties select only zero, so parameterizations are not equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameterization Failure Boundaries

children.title: Polar-Gauge Models
children.top_down_role: Dual complexity measures generated by polar bodies.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space with dual \(X^*\).
\(\rho\) is a closed convex gauge whose unit sublevel set contains the origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho^\circ\) is the support function of the primal gauge ball and controls the polar pairing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polar duality for closed convex gauges.

source_refs.locator: 2 Convex Analysis on Symmetric Matrices p. 13

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With \(B_\rho:=\{x\in X:\rho(x)\leq1\}\), define
\[
\rho^\circ(y):=\sup_{x\in B_\rho}\langle y,x\rangle,
\qquad y\in X^*.
\]
Then \(\rho^\circ\) is a closed convex gauge, possibly extended-valued, and
\[
\langle y,x\rangle\leq\rho(x)\rho^\circ(y)
\]
for all \(x\in X\) and \(y\in X^*\). Moreover, closedness gives the bipolar representation
\[
\rho(x)=\sup\{\langle y,x\rangle:\rho^\circ(y)\leq1\}.
\]
Thus polar-gauge models express primal complexity through support over a dual gauge ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar gauge is the support function of the primal unit ball, satisfies a gauge Hölder inequality, and reconstructs the closed primal gauge.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Gauge Models

source_witnesses.locator: 2 Convex Analysis on Symmetric Matrices p. 13

children.title: Antipolar Feasibility Models
children.top_down_role: Dual feasible-set geometry for gauge-constrained systems.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional space.
\(0\notin C\), and \(C\) is ray-like: \(x\in C\) and \(t\geq1\) imply \(tx\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(C'\) gives a directly checkable lower-bound certificate for every feasible point of a gauge minimization model.

notation.meaning: Polar gauge of the objective gauge.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Antipolar geometry for ray-like gauge-feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The antipolar of \(C\) is
\[
C':=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\geq1\ \text{for every }x\in C\}.
\]
For the gauge model \(\inf\{\kappa(x):x\in C\}\), any \(y\in C'\) satisfies, for every feasible \(x\),
\[
1\leq\langle y,x\rangle\leq\kappa(x)\kappa^\circ(y).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(0<\kappa^\circ(y)<+\infty\), the quantity \(1/\kappa^\circ(y)\) is a certified lower bound on the primal value. The antipolar therefore converts universal feasibility separation into a dual gauge bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The antipolar contains dual vectors pairing to at least one with every feasible point, producing verifiable lower bounds for gauge minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Antipolar Feasibility Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The antipolar definition and lower-bound formula appear correct, but this specialized gauge-duality construction has no inspectable citation. Source support is needed for the precise feasible-set assumptions and certificate formulation.

children.title: Perspective-Gauge Models
children.top_down_role: Perspective extensions accommodating nonhomogeneous fidelity terms.

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, nonnegative, and satisfies \(f(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed perspective is convex and positively homogeneous, hence is an extended-valued gauge on \(X\times\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the fidelity function.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective homogenization of a nonhomogeneous convex fidelity term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the closed perspective on \(X\times\mathbb R\) by
\[
f^\pi(z,t):=
\begin{cases}
t f(z/t),&t>0,\\
f^\infty(z),&t=0,\\
+\infty,&t<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(f^\pi\) is proper, closed, convex, nonnegative, and positively homogeneous:
\[
f^\pi(\alpha z,\alpha t)=\alpha f^\pi(z,t)\qquad(\alpha\geq0).
\]
Thus \(f^\pi\) is an extended-valued gauge and satisfies \(f(z)=f^\pi(z,1)\). Introducing the scale variable \(t\) embeds a nonhomogeneous fidelity model into homogeneous gauge geometry without discarding its original unit-scale slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective homogenizes a nonnegative convex fidelity function into an extended-valued gauge while recovering the original function at scale one.
knowledge_statements.title: Perspective-Gauge Models

children.title: Gauge Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual objects certifying optimality and exposing active gauge faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality certificate for linearly constrained gauge minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible point \(x\) and a dual vector \(y\) certify optimality when
\[
Ax=b,\qquad \kappa^\circ(A^*y)\leq1,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle=\kappa(x).
\]
Under these conditions, \(x\) minimizes \(\kappa\) over \(\{z:Az=b\}\), and
\[
A^*y\in\partial\kappa(x).
\]
If \(\kappa(x)>0\), then \(x/\kappa(x)\) belongs to the exposed face
\[
\{u:\kappa(u)\leq1,\ \langle A^*y,u\rangle=1\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and polar-feasible dual vector certify optimality when their objective values agree; when the attained gauge is positive, the dual vector also exposes the active gauge face.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\) is a closed convex gauge on a finite-dimensional space.
The primal problem \(\min\{\kappa(x):Ax=b\}\) is feasible and strong gauge duality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal-dual pair certifies optimality and, when \(\kappa(x)>0\), identifies an exposed face of the active gauge ball.

children.title: Finite Atomic Dictionaries
children.top_down_role: Finite collections of explicitly or implicitly represented atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Atomic Dictionaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient representation of a finite atomic gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B:=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). Its Minkowski gauge has the representation
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i:x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i,\ c_i\geq0\right\},
\]
where the value is \(+\infty\) if \(x\) is not in the conic hull of \(\mathcal A\). For every \(x\in X\) and \(t\geq0\),
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\leq t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in tB.
\]
Thus gauge evaluation for a finite atomic dictionary is a finite convex coefficient problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite dictionary, atomic complexity is the least total nonnegative coefficient mass needed to represent the target from its atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\subset X\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The atomic gauge equals the minimum total nonnegative coefficient mass among representations using the finite dictionary.

children.title: Continuous Atomic Families
children.top_down_role: Infinitely indexed atom sets for off-grid and measure-valued structure.

assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is compact, \(X\) is finite-dimensional, and \(a:\Theta\to X\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The atomic gauge is the least mass of a nonnegative measure whose atom integral equals the modeled point.

notation.meaning: Finite nonnegative Borel measures on the index set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure representation for compact continuously indexed atomic families.

source_refs.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mathcal A:=a(\Theta)\), the gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) admits the representation
\[
\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=
\inf\left\{\mu(\Theta):
\mu\in\mathcal M_+(\Theta),\quad
x=\int_\Theta a(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta)
\right\}.
\]
The value is \(+\infty\) when no representing measure exists. This formulation permits infinitely indexed, off-grid atoms while retaining convexity. In finite-dimensional \(X\), any feasible barycentric representation can also be replaced by one supported on finitely many indices, although the index set itself remains continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous atomic gauge is the minimum mass of a nonnegative measure representing the point as an integral of continuously indexed atoms.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Atomic Families

children.title: Centrally Symmetric Atom Sets
children.top_down_role: Atomic families closed under central reflection.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\subset X\) is compact, spans the finite-dimensional real vector space \(X\), and satisfies \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gauge of \(B\) is a norm, and its dual norm is the maximum absolute pairing with an atom.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm structure induced by a spanning centrally symmetric atom set.

source_refs.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Central symmetry gives \(B=-B\), while compactness and spanning ensure that \(B\) is a compact convex neighborhood of the origin. Consequently,
\[
\|x\|_{\mathcal A}:=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tB\}
\]
is a norm on \(X\) with unit ball \(B\). Its dual norm is
\[
\|y\|_{\mathcal A}^*
=\sup_{x\in B}\langle y,x\rangle
=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|\langle y,a\rangle|.
\]
Thus sign symmetry converts the directed atomic gauge into an even complexity measure and makes the polar support formula an absolute atom-correlation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact spanning atom set closed under sign has a symmetric convex hull whose gauge is a norm with dual given by maximum absolute atom correlation.
knowledge_statements.title: Centrally Symmetric Atom Sets

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Completed Atom Dictionaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion of a real atom dictionary under multiplication by both signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a real vector space and let \(\mathcal A_0\subset V\). Its sign completion is \(\mathcal A_{\pm}:=\mathcal A_0\cup(-\mathcal A_0)\). Consequently, every finite signed expansion \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\), with \(a_i\in\mathcal A_0\) and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\), has the nonnegative-coefficient form \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m |c_i|b_i\), where \(b_i=\operatorname{sgn}(c_i)a_i\in\mathcal A_{\pm}\); terms with \(c_i=0\) may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign completion adjoins every negative atom, converting signed atomic expansions into equivalent expansions with nonnegative coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_{\pm}=\mathcal A_0\cup(-\mathcal A_0)\) and signed coefficients can be absorbed into the atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Norm Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional atomic norm obtained from a compact, spanning, sign-symmetric family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning. Set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). Then \(C\) is compact, convex, centrally symmetric, and contains \(0\) in its interior. Its Minkowski functional \(\gamma_C(x):=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tC\}\) is a norm on \(V\), and its closed unit ball is exactly \(C\): \(\{x:\gamma_C(x)\leq1\}=C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of a compact, spanning, sign-symmetric atom family is exactly the unit ball of its Minkowski norm.

children.title: Incomplete Sign Closure
children.top_down_role: Gauge behavior caused by missing signed counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Sign Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of norm symmetry when an atomic unit set is not centrally symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(V=\mathbb R^2\), let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{e_1,e_2,-e_1,-2e_2\}\) and define \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tC\}\). The set \(C\) is compact, convex, and contains \(0\) in its interior, so \(\gamma_C\) is finite and positive definite. Nevertheless, \(C\neq-C\), and specifically \(\gamma_C(e_2)=1\) while \(\gamma_C(-e_2)=1/2\). Thus incomplete sign closure generally produces an asymmetric gauge rather than a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional atomic hull can define a finite positive gauge yet fail to be a norm when opposite atoms are missing.
assumptions_latex: \(e_1,e_2\) are the standard basis vectors of \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(e_2)\neq\gamma_C(-e_2)\), so \(\gamma_C\) is not a norm.

children.title: Directed Atom Sets

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Atom Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atom families whose coefficients are constrained to be nonnegative and whose signs carry meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a real vector space. A directed atom set is a specified subset \(\mathcal A\subset V\) used with coefficients in \(\mathbb R_+\), without requiring \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\). Its finitely generated model is \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)=\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i:m\in\mathbb N,\ c_i\geq0,\ a_i\in\mathcal A\}\). Because replacing \(a\) by \(-a\) is not automatically allowed, the orientation of each atom is part of the model specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed atom family uses only nonnegative coefficients and does not identify an atom with its negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)\) is the set of finite nonnegative atomic combinations.

notation.meaning: conic hull of the directed atoms

children.title: Conic Atom Hulls
children.top_down_role: Positive-homogeneous structures generated through conic atomic combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Atom Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the cone generated by a directed atomic family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty set \(\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^n\), its conic hull satisfies \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)=\bigcup_{m\geq1}\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i:c_i\geq0,\ a_i\in\mathcal A\}\). Equivalently, it is the smallest convex cone containing \(\mathcal A\). If \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_p\}\) and \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_p]\), then \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)=\{Ac:c\in\mathbb R_+^p\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic atom hull consists of all finite nonnegative atomic combinations and is the smallest convex cone containing the atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)\) equals the finite nonnegative-combination model; for finite \(\mathcal A\), it equals \(A\mathbb R_+^p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Restricted Gauge Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-valued atomic gauge using only nonnegative coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be nonempty, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). For \(x\in V\), define \(\gamma_C(x):=\inf\{t\geq 0:x\in tC\}\), with the infimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\). Then \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i:m\in\mathbb N,\ a_i\in\mathcal A,\ c_i\geq0,\ x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\right\}.\] Consequently, \(\gamma_C(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\notin\operatorname{cone}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed atomic gauge is the infimum of the total nonnegative coefficient mass among finite atomic representations, and it is infinite outside the generated cone.

\(\mathcal A\subset V\) is nonempty and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\).

children.title: Recession-Direction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Unbounded directions associated with directed or conic atomic sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Direction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonzero recession directions are precisely zero-cost directions of a closed convex gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex with \(0\in C\), and let \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tC\}\). Then \(\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\gamma_C(d)=0\}\). Moreover, if \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\), then \(\gamma_C(x+sd)\leq\gamma_C(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(s\geq0\). Hence a nonzero recession direction prevents positive definiteness and makes every gauge sublevel set unbounded along that direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex gauge has zero cost on recession directions; any nonzero such direction destroys positive definiteness and bounded sublevel sets.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d:\gamma_C(d)=0\}\); nonzero recession directions obstruct norm geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Image Atom Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic families and gauges transported through a linear map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:V\to W\) be linear, let \(\mathcal A\subset V\), and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). The image family is \(L\mathcal A=\{La:a\in\mathcal A\}\), and its convexified unit set is \(L(C)=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup L\mathcal A)\). For every \(y\in W\), the associated extended-valued gauge obeys \(\gamma_{L(C)}(y)=\inf\{\gamma_C(x):x\in V,\ Lx=y\}\), where the infimum over an empty fiber is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear imaging commutes with atomic convexification, and the image gauge minimizes the original gauge over each linear fiber.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(C)=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup L\mathcal A)\) and \(\gamma_{L(C)}(y)=\inf_{Lx=y}\gamma_C(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Product Atom Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product construction for atomic unit sets and their gauges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,2\), let \(C_i=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_i)\subset V_i\) be convex sets containing \(0\). Then \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A_1\times\mathcal A_2)=C_1\times C_2\). The gauge of the product satisfies \(\gamma_{C_1\times C_2}(x_1,x_2)=\max\{\gamma_{C_1}(x_1),\gamma_{C_2}(x_2)\}\), with the equality interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals. Thus Cartesian-product atomic construction produces a maximum coupling of the component gauges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexification commutes with Cartesian products, and the product gauge is the maximum of the component gauges.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Orbit Atom Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant atomic hulls generated as group orbits of seed atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a group \(G\) act linearly on a finite-dimensional real vector space \(V\), and let \(\mathcal B\subset V\) be a seed family. Define \(\mathcal A=G\mathcal B:=\{gb:g\in G,\ b\in\mathcal B\}\) and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). Then \(gC=C\) for every \(g\in G\). Consequently, the extended-valued gauge is invariant under the action: \(\gamma_C(gx)=\gamma_C(x)\) for all \(g\in G\) and \(x\in V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orbit of seed atoms has a group-invariant convex hull, whose gauge is constant along group orbits.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a group of invertible linear transformations of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(gC=C\) and \(\gamma_C(gx)=\gamma_C(x)\) for every \(g\in G\).

knowledge_statements.title: Generator Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for deleting an atom without changing a finite atomic hull or gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_p\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), fix \(j\), and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\) and \(C_{-j}=\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup(\mathcal A\setminus\{a_j\}))\). The generator \(a_j\) is redundant exactly when \(a_j\in C_{-j}\). Equivalently, \(C=C_{-j}\), in which case their extended-valued gauges agree everywhere: \(\gamma_C(x)=\gamma_{C_{-j}}(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom can be deleted without changing the hull or gauge exactly when it lies in the hull of the remaining atoms and zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_j\in C_{-j}\iff C=C_{-j}\), and then \(\gamma_C=\gamma_{C_{-j}}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Hull Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge geometry induced by convexifying an atom family together with the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be nonempty. Put \(C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\). The atomic-hull gauge is \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x):=\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in tC\}\), with value \(+\infty\) when no such \(t\) exists. Equivalently, \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\) is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the infimum of \(\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\) over finite representations \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i\) with \(c_i\geq0\) and \(a_i\in\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The atomic-hull gauge measures the least dilation of the closed convexified atom set needed to contain a point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:x\in t\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\mathcal A)\}\).

notation.meaning: closed convex atomic hull containing zero

children.title: Atomic Decomposition Models

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Decomposition Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-valued formulation containing finite nonnegative atomic combinations as finitely supported measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be compact. An atomic decomposition of \(x\in V\) is a finite positive Borel measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal A\) satisfying \[x=\int_{\mathcal A}a\,d\mu(a).\] Its atomic mass is \(\mu(\mathcal A)\), and the induced gauge is \[\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf\left\{\mu(\mathcal A):\mu\geq0,\ x=\int_{\mathcal A}a\,d\mu(a)\right\}.\] Finitely supported \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\delta_{a_i}\) yield \(x=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i a_i\) with \(c_i\geq0\). If \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\) and spans \(V\), this gauge is the atomic norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic representations are positive finite measures over the atom set; minimizing their total mass gives the atomic gauge and, for symmetric spanning atoms, a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)=\inf_{\mu\geq0}\{\mu(\mathcal A):x=\int_{\mathcal A}a\,d\mu(a)\}\).

notation.meaning: finite positive Borel measure on the atom set
atomic gauge induced by the atom set

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Faces of the atomic hull and the atoms contained in them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be compact, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). A nonempty convex set \(F\subseteq C\) is a face of \(C\) if, for every \(x,y\in C\) and every \(t\in(0,1)\), \[tx+(1-t)y\in F\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x,y\in F.\] Define its atomic content by \(\mathcal A_F=\mathcal A\cap F\). For every \(m\in\mathbb N\), if \(z\in F\) has a representation \[z=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i,\qquad a_i\in\mathcal A,\quad \lambda_i>0,\quad \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\] then \(a_i\in\mathcal A_F\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face of the atomic hull contains both endpoints whenever the relative interior of their segment meets it. Consequently, every atom with positive weight in a convex representation of a point in the face also lies in that face.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(z\in F\), \(a_i\in\mathcal A\), and \(\lambda_i>0\) with \(z=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\), one has \(a_i\in\mathcal A\cap F\) for all \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exposed Atomic Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic-hull faces selected by maximization of a linear functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be compact, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). For a nonzero linear functional \(q\in V^*\), define \[F_C(q)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C}\langle q,z\rangle.\] This set is an exposed face of \(C\). Its maximizing atoms are \[\mathcal A(q)=\left\{a\in\mathcal A:\langle q,a\rangle=\max_{b\in\mathcal A}\langle q,b\rangle\right\}.\] The maximum of the linear functional is the same over \(\mathcal A\) and \(C\), and \[F_C(q)=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A(q)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero linear functional exposes the hull points maximizing its value, and that exposed face is the convex hull of exactly the maximizing atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(q)=\operatorname{conv}\{a\in\mathcal A:\langle q,a\rangle=\max_{b\in\mathcal A}\langle q,b\rangle\}\).

notation.meaning: face of the atomic hull exposed by the functional

children.title: Active-Atom Identification

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Atom Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of atoms in a decomposition through an exposing dual functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i a_i\) with \(c_i>0\), \(a_i\in\mathcal A\), and \(t=\sum_i c_i>0\). Suppose \(q\in V^*\) satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle q,a\rangle\leq1\) and \(\langle q,x\rangle=t\). Then \[t=\sum_i c_i\langle q,a_i\rangle\leq\,\sum_i c_i=t,\] so every used atom obeys \(\langle q,a_i\rangle=1\). Thus the verifiable pair \((q,t)\) certifies that all active atoms belong to the exposed atomic set \(\{a\in\mathcal A:\langle q,a\rangle=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a dual functional is bounded by one on all atoms and attains the decomposition mass, every positively weighted atom must saturate the bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_i>0\Longrightarrow\langle q,a_i\rangle=1\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: positive weight of the ith active atom

children.title: Nonexposed Facial Structure

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexposed Facial Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of single linear certificates for nonexposed faces of atomic hulls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(\mathcal A\subset V\) be compact, set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), and let \(F\) be a face of \(C\). The face \(F\) is nonexposed precisely when there is no nonzero \(q\in V^*\) such that \[F=\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C}\langle q,z\rangle.\] Every convex decomposition into atoms of a point in \(F\) uses only atoms from \(\mathcal A\cap F\), but no single linear functional identifies exactly this face by a common maximal value. In particular, any functional whose exposed face contains \(F\) must expose a strict superset of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexposed atomic face is a genuine face that no single nonzero linear functional selects exactly, so one linear certificate cannot isolate precisely its atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(\mathcal A\subset V\) is compact and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ nonexposed}\Longleftrightarrow\nexists q\in V^*\setminus\{0\}:F=\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C}\langle q,z\rangle\).

children.title: Exact Atomic Convexification

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Atomic Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and optimizer exactness for linear optimization over atoms versus their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonempty compact set in a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(K=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), and let \(c\in V^*\). Then atomic convexification is exact for the linear problem: \[\min_{x\in K}\langle c,x\rangle=\min_{s\in S}\langle c,s\rangle.\] Moreover, \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\langle c,x\rangle=\operatorname{conv}\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in S}\langle c,s\rangle\right).\] Hence the relaxation preserves the optimal value and possesses an optimal original atom, although it may introduce additional optimal convex mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear objective, replacing a compact atom set by its convex hull preserves the optimum and retains at least one optimal atom.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is nonempty and compact in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in K}\langle c,x\rangle=\min_{s\in S}\langle c,s\rangle\).

notation.meaning: convex hull relaxation of the atomic set

children.title: Tightness Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Tightness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instancewise tightness of an atomic convex relaxation with additional constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset V\) be the structured atomic set, \(K=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), \(D\subset V\) an additional feasible set, and \(f:K\cap D\to\mathbb R\). Assume both minima are attained. The convexification is value-tight for the instance when \[\min_{x\in K\cap D}f(x)=\min_{x\in S\cap D}f(x).\] It is solution-tight when additionally \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K\cap D}f(x)\subseteq S\cap D.\] A family of instances forms a tightness regime when the corresponding equality, and if required the inclusion, holds for every instance in that family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is value-tight when every relaxed optimum value matches the structured problem, and solution-tight when every relaxed optimizer is structured.
assumptions_latex: \(S\cap D\) and \(K\cap D\) are nonempty, with \(K=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
The displayed minima of \(f\) are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{cvx}}=p_{\mathrm{str}}\), with solution tightness requiring \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{K\cap D}f\subseteq S\cap D\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of the structured set

children.title: Convexification Gaps

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value loss caused by replacing a structured feasible set with its convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset V\), let \(K=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), and let \(D\subset V\). For a minimization objective \(f\) whose two infima are finite, define \[p_{\mathrm{str}}=\inf_{x\in S\cap D}f(x),\qquad p_{\mathrm{cvx}}=\inf_{x\in K\cap D}f(x).\] Since \(S\cap D\subseteq K\cap D\), the additive convexification gap is \[\Delta_{m cvx}=p_{\mathrm{str}}-p_{\mathrm{cvx}}\geq0.\] The relaxation is value-tight exactly when \(\Delta_{m cvx}=0\); a positive gap records an objective value attainable only after convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convexification gap is the structured optimum minus the relaxed optimum; it is nonnegative for minimization and vanishes exactly under value tightness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{\rm cvx}=p_{\mathrm{str}}-p_{\mathrm{cvx}}\geq0\), and \(\Delta_{\rm cvx}=0\iff p_{\mathrm{str}}=p_{\mathrm{cvx}}\).

notation.meaning: optimal value over the structured feasible set

children.title: Lost Structural Distinctions

knowledge_statements.title: Lost Structural Distinctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct atomic mixtures can collapse to the same point after convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(V=\mathbb R^2\), take \(\mathcal A=\{e_1,-e_1,e_2,-e_2\}\). The two probability measures \[\mu_1=\tfrac12\delta_{e_1}+\tfrac12\delta_{-e_1},\qquad \mu_2=\tfrac12\delta_{e_2}+\tfrac12\delta_{-e_2}\] have disjoint supports but the same barycenter: \[\int_{\mathcal A}a\,d\mu_1(a)=0=\int_{\mathcal A}a\,d\mu_2(a).\] Thus the convexified variable \(x=0\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) cannot determine which active-atom pair generated it. Convexification preserves the barycenter while discarding decomposition support and latent structural labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite horizontal atoms and opposite vertical atoms both average to zero, so the convexified point cannot reveal which distinct atom pair generated it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_1\neq\mu_2\) but \(\int a\,d\mu_1(a)=\int a\,d\mu_2(a)=0\).

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at atom a
standard coordinate vectors in the plane

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct, self-contained, and appropriately typed, but the claimed structural interpretation lacks a cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Atomic-Norm Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless recovery by minimizing atomic norm over an affine measurement fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a linear map \(\Phi:V\to Y\), exact data \(y\in Y\), and a compact centrally symmetric spanning atom set \(\mathcal A\subset V\). Form its atomic norm \(\|x\|_{\mathcal A}=\gamma_{\mathcal A}(x)\) and solve \[\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in V}\ \|x\|_{\mathcal A}\quad\text{subject to}\quad\Phi x=y.\] If the feasible set is nonempty, output any minimizer \(\widehat x\); otherwise report infeasibility. Exact recovery of a target \(x_0\) means that \(x_0\) is the unique minimizer when \(y=\Phi x_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover noiseless data by selecting the smallest atomic-norm point in the measurement fiber; recovery is exact when the true point is the unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(\mathcal A\subset V\) is compact, centrally symmetric, and spans \(V\).

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Norm Constrained Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex estimation under a fixed atomic-complexity budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input observations \(y\), a convex lower-semicontinuous loss \(L_y:V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), an atomic norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\), and a budget \(\tau\geq0\). Solve \[\widehat x_\tau\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in V}L_y(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|x\|_{\mathcal A}\leq\tau.\] Output any minimizer when one exists. For a linear observation model with squared loss, use \(L_y(x)=\tfrac12\|\Phi x-y\|_2^2\). The parameter \(\tau\) fixes the admissible atomic complexity independently of the achieved data fit.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Norm Penalized Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex estimation trading data fit against atomic complexity through a penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input observations \(y\), a proper convex lower-semicontinuous loss \(L_y:V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), an atomic norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\), and \(\lambda>0\). Solve \[\widehat x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in V}\left\{L_y(x)+\lambda\|x\|_{\mathcal A}\right\}.\] Output any minimizer when one exists. With a linear observation operator and squared loss, this becomes \[\widehat x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in V}\left\{\tfrac12\|\Phi x-y\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_{\mathcal A}\right\}.\] Larger \(\lambda\) assigns greater optimization weight to low atomic complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate by minimizing convex data loss plus a positive multiple of the atomic norm; the tuning parameter controls the fit-complexity tradeoff.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite-dimensional and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\) is an atomic norm.

children.title: Atomic-Norm Denoising

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Norm Denoising
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalized least-squares denoising over a finite-dimensional atomic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space and let \(\mathcal A\subset H\) be compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning. Its atomic norm is the gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\). Given data \(y=x_0+w\in H\) and a parameter \(\lambda>0\), atomic-norm denoising returns any solution
\[
\widehat x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{\frac12\lVert y-x\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\right\}.
\]
The quadratic term measures agreement with the noisy observation, while the atomic norm favors representations using few atoms. The objective is strongly convex, so \(\widehat x_\lambda\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic-norm denoising minimizes squared data error plus an atomic-norm penalty; in finite dimensions its strongly convex objective has a unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(\mathcal A\subset H\) is compact, centrally symmetric, and spans \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\{\tfrac12\lVert y-x\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\}\) exists and is unique.

children.title: Dual Atomic Norms
children.top_down_role: Polar complexity measures associated with atomic hulls.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Atomic Norms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar norm associated with a centrally symmetric atomic hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and let \(\mathcal A\subset H\) be compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning. If \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathcal A}\) is the gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\), then its dual atomic norm is
\[
\lVert z\rVert_{\mathcal A}^{*}=\sup_{\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\le 1}\langle z,x\rangle=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle.
\]
Consequently, Hölder duality gives \(\langle z,x\rangle\le \lVert z\rVert_{\mathcal A}^{*}\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\), and the dual unit ball is the polar of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual atomic norm is the largest correlation with an atom, equivalently the support function of the atomic hull.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is compact, centrally symmetric, and spanning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert z\rVert_{\mathcal A}^{*}=\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle z,a\rangle\) and \(\langle z,x\rangle\le\lVert z\rVert_{\mathcal A}^{*}\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\).

notation.meaning: Norm dual to the atomic norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Face Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A dual vector exposes the atomic face supporting an optimal decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\ne0\) admit an atomic decomposition \(x=\sum_{j=1}^{r}c_j a_j\) with \(c_j>0\), \(a_j\in\mathcal A\), and \(\sum_jc_j=\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\). A vector \(q\) is an atomic-face certificate when
\[
\lVert q\rVert_{
\mathcal A}^{*}\le1,
\qquad \langle q,x\rangle=\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}.
\]
Then every active atom satisfies \(\langle q,a_j\rangle=1\), hence lies in the exposed face \(F_q=\{a\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A):\langle q,a\rangle=1\}\). Moreover, \(q\in\partial\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\), so checking dual feasibility and equality certifies that the decomposition uses only atoms on \(F_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible vector attaining equality at the signal exposes a face containing every atom in any compatible optimal positive decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) defines an atomic norm on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\in\partial\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\) and \(a_j\in F_q\) for every active atom.

Subdifferential of the atomic norm at the signal.

children.title: Dual Interpolant Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Interpolant Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-atom certificate interpolating active phases and bounded elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a:T\to H\) be a continuous complex atomic family, let \(x_0=\sum_{j=1}^{s}c_j a(t_j)\) with distinct \(t_j\in T\) and nonzero \(c_j\), and let measurements be generated by \(\Phi:H\to Y\). A dual interpolant certificate is a vector \(q=\Phi^{*}p\) whose correlation function \(Q(t)=\langle q,a(t)\rangle\) obeys
\[
Q(t_j)=\frac{c_j}{|c_j|}\quad(1\le j\le s),

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Polynomial Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trigonometric-polynomial specialization for line-spectral atomic recovery.

For \(n\) consecutive Fourier samples, define \(a(f)=(1,e^{2\pi i f},\ldots,e^{2\pi i(n-1)f})\) for \(f\in[0,1)\). Given coefficients \(c_j\ne0\) at distinct frequencies \(f_j\), a dual polynomial certificate is
\[
Q(f)=\langle q,a(f)\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\overline{q_k}e^{2\pi i kf}
\]
with \(Q(f_j)=c_j/|c_j|\) and \(|Q(f)|<1\) for every \(f\notin\{f_1,\ldots,f_s\}\). If \(q\) belongs to the range of the measurement adjoint, these inequalities certify dual feasibility and uniquely expose the spectral atoms under injectivity on their span.

assumptions_latex: The atoms are length-\(n\) complex Fourier vectors.
The measurement map is injective on the active atomic span.

children.title: Off-Support Control
children.top_down_role: Certificate behavior away from active parameter locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Off-Support Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dual separation of active atoms, with uniform margins only away from the active parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be a parameter space, let \(S=\{t_1,\ldots,t_s\}\subset T\) be the active parameter set, and let \(Q(t)=\langle q,a(t)\rangle\) be a dual correlation function that interpolates the required phases or signs on \(S\). Strict off-support control is the pointwise condition
\[
|Q(t)|<1\qquad\text{for every }t\in T\setminus S.
\]
For a subset \(E\subseteq T\setminus S\), a quantitative margin \(\eta>0\) on \(E\) means
\[
\sup_{t\in E}|Q(t)|\le 1-\eta.
\]
When \(Q\) is continuous and points of \(T\setminus S\) approach an active point where \(|Q|=1\), no positive uniform margin can hold on all of \(T\setminus S\). Pointwise strict control ensures that no inactive parameter attains dual modulus one; without strictness, dual feasibility may certify optimality without isolating the active parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Off-support control requires the dual correlation to have magnitude strictly below one at every inactive parameter. A positive uniform margin can generally be required only on regions separated from the active parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the atom-parameter domain and \(S\subset T\) is the finite active set.
\(Q(t)=\langle q,a(t)\rangle\) interpolates the prescribed phases or signs on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|Q(t)|<1\) for every \(t\in T\setminus S\) prevents inactive parameters from attaining dual modulus one; a bound \(\sup_{t\in E}|Q(t)|\le1-\eta\) requires a specified set \(E\subseteq T\setminus S\).

notation.meaning: Off-support region on which a uniform margin is imposed.
Positive uniform separation margin on the specified region.

children.title: Certificate Representability Limits
children.top_down_role: Continuous atomic settings lacking the required certificate representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Representability Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery certificates are restricted by the measurement-adjoint range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained problem \(\min_x\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}\) subject to \(\Phi x=\Phi x_0\), every Lagrange dual certificate representable from the data has the form \(q=\Phi^{*}p\). Therefore a necessary KKT condition for certifying optimality of \(x_0\) is
\[
\operatorname{range}(\Phi^{*})\cap\partial\lVert x_0\rVert_{\mathcal A}\ne\varnothing.
\]
If this intersection is empty, no measurement-representable dual certificate can establish optimality. If the intersection is nonempty but contains no vector with strict off-support control, ordinary subgradient certificates may establish optimality but cannot, by strict exposure alone, certify uniqueness or exact active-atom identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate must lie in both the measurement-adjoint range and the atomic-norm subdifferential; an empty intersection makes such certification impossible.
assumptions_latex: The recovery problem has exact linear equality constraints.
The atomic norm is proper and finite on the ambient finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(\Phi^{*})\cap\partial\lVert x_0\rVert_{\mathcal A}=\varnothing\) rules out any measurement-representable KKT certificate.

notation.meaning: Set of dual vectors representable through measurements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adjoint-range/subdifferential intersection is the appropriate representability boundary and the failure-boundary kind fits, but its KKT formulation and claims about uniqueness certification lack a cited source.

children.title: Atomic Decomposition Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity among atomic representations of the same modeled object.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Decomposition Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete atomic norm with two distinct norm-attaining decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In \(\mathbb R^2\), let
\[
\mathcal A=\left\{\pm(1,0),\,\pm(0,1),\,\pm\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)\right\}
\]
and let \(x=(1,1)\). Then
\[
x=(1,0)+(0,1)=2\left(\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
Both positive decompositions have coefficient sum \(2\). Moreover, the linear functional \(q=(1,1)\) satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\langle q,a\rangle=1\) and \(\langle q,x\rangle=2\), so \(\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}=2\). Thus both decompositions attain the atomic norm, demonstrating that the modeled object and its atomic norm can be unique while its norm-minimizing atomic decomposition is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vector (1,1) has two distinct norm-attaining decompositions under an atomic set containing both coordinate atoms and their midpoint.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is \(\mathbb R^2\) with its standard inner product.
The atomic norm is the gauge of \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert(1,1)\rVert_{\mathcal A}=2\), attained by two distinct atomic decompositions.

notation.meaning: Specified symmetric atomic set in two dimensions.
Dual vector certifying the atomic norm value.

children.title: Coordinate ℓ1 Models

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate ℓ1 Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic representation of ordinary coordinate sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In \(\mathbb R^n\), take the coordinate atomic set \(\mathcal A=\{\pm e_i:1\le i\le n\}\), where \(e_i\) is the \(i\)-th standard basis vector. Its atomic hull is the cross-polytope, and its gauge satisfies
\[
\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}=\inf\left\{\sum_j c_j:x=\sum_jc_ja_j,
\ c_j\ge0,
\ a_j\in\mathcal A\right\}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i|=\lVert x\rVert_1.
\]
Accordingly, coordinate-sparse vectors are modeled by a small number of active coordinate atoms, while the convex low-complexity surrogate is the ordinary \(\ell_1\) norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using signed coordinate vectors as atoms makes the atomic norm exactly the ordinary ℓ1 norm and models coordinate sparsity.
assumptions_latex: The atoms are the signed standard basis vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x\rVert_{\mathcal A}=\lVert x\rVert_1=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i|\).

children.title: Synthesis Dictionary Models
children.top_down_role: Sparse representations through combinations of dictionary elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Synthesis Dictionary Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse coefficients synthesize signals through a fixed dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^n\) be a fixed dictionary with columns \(d_1,
\ldots,d_p\). The synthesis \(s\)-sparse model is
\[
\mathcal M_s(D)=\{D\alpha:\alpha\in\mathbb R^p,
\lVert\alpha\rVert_0\le s\}.
\]
Its convex synthesis gauge is
\[
R_D(x)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^p}\{\lVert\alpha\rVert_1:D\alpha=x\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when \(x\notin\operatorname{range}(D)\). If the columns are normalized and their signs are included, \(R_D\) is the atomic gauge generated by \(\{\pm d_j\}_{j=1}^{p}\). Different sparse coefficient vectors may synthesize the same signal when \(D\) is redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synthesis model represents signals as dictionary combinations with sparse coefficients; minimizing coefficient ℓ1 norm yields the associated convex gauge.
assumptions_latex: Dictionary columns are normalized when identified with atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M_s(D)=\{D\alpha:\lVert\alpha\rVert_0\le s\}\) and \(R_D(x)=\inf_{D\alpha=x}\lVert\alpha\rVert_1\).

children.title: Analysis Cosparse Models
children.top_down_role: Low-complexity models based on sparse transformed responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Analysis Cosparse Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signals having many zero responses under a fixed analysis operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) be a fixed analysis operator. A vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is \(\ell\)-cosparse with respect to \(\Omega\) when at least \(\ell\) coordinates of \(\Omega x\) vanish:
\[
\#\{i:(\Omega x)_i=0\}\ge\ell,
\]
equivalently \(\lVert\Omega x\rVert_0\le p-\ell\). For a cosupport \(\Lambda\subseteq\{1,
\ldots,p\}\), the corresponding subspace is \(\ker(\Omega_\Lambda)\); hence the model is a union of such subspaces. The standard convex analysis regularizer is \(x\mapsto\lVert\Omega x\rVert_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analysis-cosparse signal has many zero entries after applying an analysis operator; fixed cosupports define subspaces, and analysis ℓ1 is the convex surrogate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is \(\ell\)-cosparse exactly when \(\lVert\Omega x\rVert_0\le p-\ell\).

notation.meaning: Index set of vanishing analysis coefficients.

children.title: Fixed Weighted ℓ1 Models

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Weighted ℓ1 Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate sparsity with predetermined positive penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w=(w_1,
\ldots,w_n)\in(0,
\infty)^n\) be fixed independently of the optimization variable and observed noise realization. The fixed weighted \(\ell_1\) norm is
\[
\lVert x\rVert_{1,w}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_i|x_i|.
\]
It is the atomic norm generated by \(\mathcal A_w=\{\pm e_i/w_i:1\le i\le n\}\), and its dual norm is
\[
\lVert z\rVert_{*,w}=\max_{1\le i\le n}\frac{|z_i|}{w_i}.
\]
Strict positivity and finiteness of every weight make the penalty a norm; zero or infinite weights instead produce degeneracy or hard coordinate restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed positive coordinate weights define a weighted ℓ1 norm whose atoms are rescaled basis vectors and whose dual is a weighted maximum norm.
assumptions_latex: The weights are fixed before solving the optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x\rVert_{1,w}=\sum_iw_i|x_i|\) and \(\lVert z\rVert_{*,w}=\max_i|z_i|/w_i\).

notation.meaning: Fixed positive penalty on coordinate i.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(f:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and bounded below, choose \(\lambda>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), and take \(x^{(0)}\in\operatorname{dom}f\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), set \[w_j^{(k+1)}=\frac{1}{|x_j^{(k)}|+\varepsilon}\quad(j=1,\ldots,p),\] and choose \[x^{(k+1)}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^p}\left\{f(x)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p w_j^{(k+1)}|x_j|\right\}.\] Stop according to a prescribed termination rule and return the last iterate. Each subproblem is convex, although the adaptive iteration as a whole is not a single jointly convex optimization problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb{N}\). For \(w\in[0,\infty)^p\), define \(J_w(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p w_j|x_j|\) for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^p\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(\mathcal{G}\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\) into nonempty groups, and let \(d_g>0\) for every \(g\in\mathcal{G}\).
